summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as an ESLint processors stub (dist/index.js exports a trivial `preprocess: () => ['']`), but its package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is control-flow-obfuscated and, at npm install, locates or downloads the Bun runtime from oven-sh/bun GitHub releases into a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes the sibling file math_init.js under Bun via execFileSync. math_init.js is a ~727 KB Bun-bundled file (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) with hex-mangled identifiers, a shuffled string/number constant array, and a rotator function — an opaque payload with no source form. Executing under Bun rather than Node evades Node-oriented install-time inspection. The install-time behavior is unrelated to the advertised ESLint stub functionality, and the scoped name `@servicetitan/eslint-plugin-processors-stub` mirrors the shape of an internal ServiceTitan tooling package (repo field points to github.com/servicetitan/uikit), consistent with a dependency-confusion / scoped-name impersonation targeting ServiceTitan developers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
